lawyer:
Md. Hannan and Khaled Ahmed, Advocates —For the Appellants 
Fida Kamal with Masuma Akhtar and Idris Khan, Advocates—For the Respondents.
parties:
Abdul Ghani Sheikh ----- Appellant
Vs.
Jagadish Chandra Mridha and others ----- Respondents
full_judgment:
Syed JR Mudassir Husain J: This Appeal, at the instance of the defendant No.1, the Gotapara Union Matshyajibi Samabaya Samity Ltd. is directed against an order dated 8-5-1994 passed by the Subordinate Judge Bagerhat, in Civil Suit No.24 of 1994 granting temporary injunction against the appellant and others restraining them from dispossessing the plaintiff respondent from 8 'Kha' schedule of suit fishery. 

 2. The short facts giving rise to this appeal are that, the respondent instituted Title Suit No. 24 of 1994 for a declaration that the agreement dated 30-5-92 executed between the plaintiff and the said defendant No. 1 for joint enjoyment of the suit fishery known as Kuramara Fishery is according to law and it is binding upon the defendant Nos. 1-4 and they are bound to abide by the terms of the said agreement. 

 3. The case of the respondent is that they applied for lease of the said fishery for 10 years from 1399 BS to 1408 BS and the appellant society was also an applicant for the lease of the said fishery for 4 years from 1399 BS to 1408 BS. Both the societies are located in the same area and in order to avoid the clash between them the Foreign Minister and the local MP intervened in the matter by persuading them to enjoy the fishery jointly at the ratio of 8 annas portion for the appellant society, 4 annas portion for the plaintiffs society and the remaining 4 annas portion for another local society. An agreement to that effect was reached between them on 30-5-92. It was also stated that the respondent also filed an application to the Minister concerned for joint enjoyment of the fishery. But the Ministry of Land granted case of the suit fishery to the defendant No.1 the Gotapara Union Matshyajibi Samity for the year 1399 BS to 1401 BS vide order Bhu, MA /7-Bager-3/91 /450 dated 24-6-92. The further case of the respondent is that as per terms of the said agreement between the parties the respondent society was given possession of "Kha" schedule fishery for enjoyment against payment of rent of its portion. After some time a trouble arose between them and the plaintiff respondent was threatened with dispossession from his portion of the suit fishery, hence the suit was filed. 

 4. The respondent thereafter filed an application for temporary injunction under Order 39 rules 1 and 2 read with section 151 of the Code of Civil Procedure to restrain the defendants 1-6 from dispossessing him from the said "Kha" schedule of the said fishery till disposal of the suit. The defendant appellant resisted the said application by filing written objection thereto and denied all the material allegations made therein. The appellant's case is that defendant No.4 Basharat Howlader the then Secretary of the appellant Matshyajibi Samabaya Samity was not entitled to enter into any agreement with anybody and the said defendant No. 4 contested for the post of Secretary again in the election of appellant society but was defeated and he then became instrumental in doing harm to the defendant society and with that end in view it was the defendant No. 4 who got the suit filed by the plaintiff with malafide intention. The appellant further stated that it was their society alone which was granted settlement of the suit fishery by the Ministry concerned on 24-6-92 and lease deed was duly executed between the said lessor and the lessee. In such view of the matter the plaintiff has no legal right in the suit fishery and there is no prima facie case in his favour. It is further stated that the plaintiff's suit is not maintainable and his prayer for injunction is liable to be rejected. 

 5. The learned Subordinate Judge granted temporary injunction against the appellant and ex parte against the rest restraining them from dispossessing the plaintiff from the "Kha" schedule of the fishery till disposal of the suit by the impugned order as aforesaid. 

 7. Mr. Hannan, the learned Advocate appearing for the appellant,placed before us the relevant papers and taken us through the plaint, application for injunction, written objection thereto, the lease deed between the appellant and the Government and other connected papers as well as the impugned order. The learned lawyer for the appellant firstly submits that it is the appellant society alone who was granted lease of the suit fishery and a bilateral deed of lease was duly executed between the parties and as such the prima facie right, title and possession are all in favour of the appellant and the respondent has no legal right to file the suit. Mr. Hannan thus argued that the learned Subordinate Judge erred in law in granting temporary injunction against the appellant without considering the fact that the alleged agreement dated 30-5-92 between the appellant Society and the plaintiff respondent has no legal validity and the respondent acquires no legal right to enforce the said agreement in the eye of law in asmuch as the enforcement of such an illegal agreement would tantamount to a sub-lease to the plaintiff by the lease-holder appellant defeating the provision of clause 10 of the bilateral lease deed. Mr. Hannan has further argued that the plaintiff's alleged claim in a portion of the suit fishery as a partner with the appellant by the said agreement is not to say a private arrangement and it has no legal basis which can neither establish any legal right nor establish a prima facie case for injunction. The learned Subordinate Judge, having thus misdirected himself, failed to apply his judicial mind in finding prima facie case in favour of the respondent which is erroneous and the order of injunction cannot be sustained. 

 9. Mr. Fida Kamal, the learned Advocate appearing for the respondent, on the other hand, contends that the appellant was a party to the resolution taken on 30-7-92 in order to approve the said agreement dated 30-5-92 so far the plaintiffs 4 annas share in the suit fishery and as such the said agreement is binding and the same can be enforced against the appellant and he cannot deny the same and the appellant is estopped by the principle of promissory estoppel. Mr. Fida Kamal has next contended that a plea of sub-lease as taken by the appellant is misconceived idea because the agreement entered into between the parties is an arrangement intending to create legal relation between them and it is not a sub-lease as contemplated under the clause 10 of the lease deed. In support of his contention the learned Advocate for the respondent has referred to a decision in the case of Secretary, Ministry of Industries, Nationalised Industries Division. vs. Saleh Ahmed and another and Bangladesh Textile Mills Corporation vs. Saleh Ahmed and others reported in 46 DLR (AD) page 148. We will discuss the decision in appropriate place of this judgment. 

 11. The only point that calls for determination in the instant appeal is whether the plaintiff respondent has acquired any right in the portion of the suit fishery on the basis of the agreement dated 30-5-92. 

 13. The said clause 10 of the lease deed clearly prohibits sub-leasing of fishery with anyone else, in such circumstances therefore, we hold that the said agreement is not a contract in the eye of law as all contracts are agreement but all agreements are not contracts. This much can be said that the alleged agreement between the parties is at best a sort of private arrangement between them. In case of any disagreement or dispute arising out of the said agreement it may be a breach of promise of the terms thereof but it cannot create any legal relation between them. The alleged agreement as we have already held is a private arrangement and has no legal validity. However, for the breach of any of the terms of the said agreement the plaintiff has remedy in claiming damages but not injunction. 

 15. In the instant case it appears that the defendant society (appellant) is a bonafide lease holder of the fishery in question with a notice to the plaintiff (respondent), as such, the plaintiff, in our opinion, cannot have any legal right to establish a strong prima facie case in his favour. The appellants having been put into possession of the entire suit fishery, the prima facie case, balance of convenience and inconvenience are in favour of the appellant. The plaintiff will not suffer any irreparable loss and injury if the injunction is not granted rather it is the appellant who is likely to suffer irreparable loss and injury if restrained from enjoyment of the fishery. The plaintiff even if paid money in respect of his portion of the fishery on the basis of the said agreement and being in possession of the part of the fishery is not without any remedy; he can very well claim damages against the appellant acting inconsistently and for any breach of the said agreement. We are further of opinion that in view of the clause 10 of the lease deed, the appellant society had no power to take a decision in whatever manner to part with any portion of the suit fishery with any party under an agreement based on no legal footing can be enforced. The appellant is not under any legal obligation to perform his duty towards the respondent. We thus hold that the said agreement is nothing but a sub-lease prohibited by law as laid down in clause 10 of the lease deed and we further hold that the denial Of the plaintiff's right in the suit fishery cannot be treated as binding on the appellant and the question of the principle of promissory estoppel does not arise, in view of the aforesaid facts and circumstance of the present case. The observation of Lord Denning, in the case of Central London Property Trust Ltd. vs. High Trees House Ltd. as quoted in paragraph 8 of the said reported decision is of no help to Mr. Fida Kamal as relied by him. The facts of the cited case and those of the present are also distinguishable and cannot be applied in the instant case. Even for argument sake if the said agreement dated 30-5-92 is regarded as a contract we hold that the same cannot be enforced as it is an illegal agreement and its enforcement would tantamount to a sub-lease defeating the provision of the clause 10 of the lease deed as we have already considered the said aspect and therefore no injunction can be granted and damage is available against the appellant as also pointed earlier. As regards merit of the case we find that the impugned order suffers from legal infirmity as the learned Subordinate Judge failed to discuss the appellant's case with reference to documents filed by the appellant. Injunction is a form of equitable relief and before it is granted the applicant must satisfy the court that there is a complete contract upon which the plaintiff claims to have acquired a right. But the impugned order of the learned Subordinate Judge does not reflect as to how he was satisfied upon consideration of the case of the parties to arrive at his findings and decisions. In a case of granting temporary injunction plaintiff is not only to establish his strong prima facie case but also to show that he will suffer irreparable loss and injury and will be inconvenienced if injunction is not granted. From the above discussion we do not find that plaintiff was able to prove that he has strong prima facie case and if injunction is not granted he will suffer irreparable loss and there will be great inconvenience caused to him. We are further constrained to hold that it is the appellant who will be seriously prejudiced if the said agreement is allowed to be enforced as the very lease of the entire fishery would be liable to be cancelled as per clause 10 of the lease deed.
